eyebrow: Before — nobody can tell what this means
code:
d = pd.DataFrame({"s": [...], "q": [...], "p": [...]})
x = d[d.s == "c"]
x["t"] = x.q * x.p * 0.92
# also triggers SettingWithCopyWarning!
caption: s, q, p, and 0.92 mean nothing on their own — and x is an unsafe slice of d.

eyebrow: After — names, a constant, a function
code:
LOYALTY_DISCOUNT = 0.92  # 8% off for loyalty members

def add_order_total(df):
    """Return a copy of df with an order_total column."""
    out = df.copy()
    out["order_total"] = out["quantity"] * out["unit_price"] * LOYALTY_DISCOUNT
    return out
caption: Three changes: descriptive names, a named constant with a comment, and a function that copies its input.
